lessons.title: Role and Functions of an Operating System
lessons.concept: An operating system (OS) is system software that manages hardware resources and provides services to applications. Core functions include process management, memory management, file system management, device (I/O) management, and providing a user interface.
lessons.formula: OS responsibilities: process + memory + storage/files + I/O devices + security/protection + user/program interface.
lessons.worked_example: When you open a program, the OS creates/loads a process, allocates memory, schedules CPU time, and handles file/device access needed by that program.
mistakes: Confusing the OS with application software
Thinking the OS only provides a graphical interface
Ignoring resource management as a central OS role

lessons.title: Processes, Threads, and CPU Scheduling
lessons.concept: A process is a program in execution with its own address space and resources. A thread is a lightweight unit of execution within a process. The CPU scheduler selects which ready process/thread runs, aiming for fairness, responsiveness, and efficient CPU utilization. Common states include new, ready, running, waiting/blocked, and terminated.
lessons.formula: Basic cycle: ready -> running (scheduled) -> waiting/ready/terminated depending on events.
lessons.worked_example: If a running process requests disk I/O, it may move to waiting/blocked state; the scheduler picks another ready process to run so the CPU is not idle.
mistakes: Confusing a program (passive) with a process (active)
Assuming only one process can exist in memory at a time on multitasking systems
Mixing up process states and their transitions

lessons.title: Memory Management and File System Basics
lessons.concept: Memory management controls allocation of RAM to processes, providing isolation and efficient use (techniques include paging/virtual memory at a high level). The file system organizes data into files/directories on storage and manages access, naming, and metadata. Both are key OS services for safe and organized resource use.
lessons.formula: Memory: allocate/protect/track; File system: create/read/write/delete files + organize directories + manage permissions/metadata.
lessons.worked_example: Virtual memory allows a system to run processes whose total memory demand exceeds physical RAM by using disk space as backing storage (with performance trade-offs). A file system maps file names to stored data blocks on disk.
mistakes: Assuming RAM and disk serve the same role with no distinction
Believing file organization is handled by hardware rather than the OS/file system
